Introduction

St. Lawrence was an archdeacon of Rome, remembered for care of the poor and martyrdom during the persecution under Valerian.

Death / martyrdom

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Lawrence, also spelled Laurence, served as archdeacon in the Church of Rome during the third-century persecution under Valerian. The OCA commemorates him with fellow Roman martyrs and places their suffering in 258.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening identification and date

Life and notable events

In the received life, his imprisoned bishop entrusts the Church’s valuables to him for distribution to people in need. When officials demand the treasury, St. Lawrence brings poor people before them. The story makes his diaconal responsibility for charitable service central to his witness.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Distribution of treasures and presentation of the poor

Martyrdom

The OCA account says that he refuses to sacrifice to idols and undergoes repeated torture. It describes his final execution on a heated iron gridiron on August 10, 258. The details are presented as the Church’s received martyrdom narrative; this profile introduces no new speech or reconstructed dialogue.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Trial, tortures and final execution

Commemoration and legacy

The life recounts the honorable burial of his body and the later presence of relics in Rome and other Orthodox locations. His Orthodox commemoration brings an early western martyr into the same calendar of witness as the martyrs of the East.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Burial and relics; commemoration heading
